review_notes:
I read the whole file and compared the proofs of every theorem. The closest repetition is in `mgf_intCast_skellamMeasure` and `charFun_map_intCast_skellamMeasure`. Both push the measure forward to the difference of two Poisson laws. Both then rewrite `f (z.1 - z.2)` as a product of one-variable exponentials with a `funext`/`← exp_add`/`congr 1`/`ring` block. Both finish with `integral_prod_mul` and the Poisson transform lemma. `integrable_exp_mul_intCast_skellamMeasure` has the same algebraic factorisation.

I could not justify a finding. The shared pattern is a short algebraic rewrite plus one call to `integral_prod_mul`. A generic helper lemma would need an `RCLike` or ℂ-valued multiplicative-factorisation hypothesis. Each caller would then supply that same hypothesis, so the rewritten uses would save little and the helper would add its own API surface. The real versus complex coercion handling (`push_cast`, `Complex.ofReal_neg`) also differs between the two proofs. That falls under the rubric's short calculations and routine unfolding.

The other proofs are not duplicates of each other. The mean and variance proofs use different derivative facts. The convolution proof reduces to characteristic functions once. I did not run any replacement through Lean, so I make no claim that one would compile.
